title: Five9 Pricing in 2026: Core at $159, a 50-Seat Minimum and Quoted Plans
summary: Five9 lists Digital at $119 and Core at $159 per concurrent user a month, with a 50-seat minimum. Plus, Pro and Enterprise are quoted. See what adds cost.
body_markdown:
Five9 publishes two prices. Its pricing page lists Digital at $119 and Core at $159 per concurrent user a month, with a minimum of 50 seats. Digital covers chat, email, SMS and social messaging without voice. Core adds voice. Plus, Pro and Enterprise show no price and are quoted by sales. Usage-based charges may apply. No free trial is listed. Read on November 17, 2026.


Trellus publishes this guide and sells competing calling software. Every Five9 detail below comes from Five9's own pricing page, product pages and documentation, opened on November 17, 2026. No price here comes from a review site, and no Five9 account was used or tested. For a side-by-side view, see the Trellus Call Center and Five9 comparison on the[call center page](https://www.trellus.ai/call-center) .


## Five9 pricing at a glance


Five9's[pricing page](https://www.five9.com/pricing) lists five bundles. Two have a price. Each bundle has a quote button, and the page shows no way to buy online.


Five9 bundles in US dollars, as listed on Five9's own pricing page and read on November 17, 2026. Prices are per concurrent user. The page shows one monthly figure per seat and no separate annual price. Bundle Published price Seat minimum Free trial What is included


Digital $119 a seat a month 50 seats None listed Chat, email, SMS and MMS, social messaging, agent desktop, recording. No voice, no AI features, no CRM or UC adapter


Core $159 a seat a month 50 seats None listed Voice plus the digital channels, dialer, blended inbound and outbound, AI Summaries, Live Transcription, AI Insights, a CRM and a UC adapter


Plus Not published; quoted Not stated separately None listed Core plus AI Agent Assist and AI Knowledge


Pro Not published; quoted Not stated separately None listed Core plus workforce engagement: quality management, workforce management and analytics


Enterprise Not published; quoted Not stated separately None listed Everything in Plus and Pro together


The 50-seat minimum comes from a note under the bundles. It says the prices above are per concurrent user, that usage-based pricing may apply, and that the minimum is 50 seats. The same note says Five9 also sells custom quotes and pricing based on named agents or pay per use. The page marks the dialer as included in every bundle, Digital among them.


At list price, 50 Core seats come to $7,950 a month, and 50 Digital seats come to $5,950. That is arithmetic from the page, not a quote, and it leaves out usage.


## What changes the real cost of Five9


The seat price is the start. The count of seats, usage, named licenses and add-ons all move the bill, and most of them have no public price.


### What a concurrent user means


Five9 prices by concurrent user, not by named person. Its documentation gives a plain example: a domain with 10 licenses lets 10 agents log in at the same time, and the 11th agent to try gets an error. That[knowledge article](https://documentation.five9.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-knowledgearticles2/page/kA61W000000Xa0ESAS.html) was last updated on October 28, 2026.


So a team buys seats for its busiest moment, not for its headcount. As an illustration, a center with 80 agents across shifts and no more than 50 logged in at once would need 50 concurrent seats. A team where everyone works the same hours gets no saving from this model.


### Named licenses for workforce tools


Workforce engagement tools are licensed differently. A footnote on the pricing page says they are offered on a named basis, and that extra named seats are sold as add-ons when a customer needs more of them than the concurrent seats it bought.


Five9's[workforce management article](https://documentation.five9.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-knowledgearticles1/page/kA6TN0000006gqz0AA.html) says each concurrent user license includes one named user license for each workforce product purchased, and that named licenses cannot be shared. In the 80-agent example, 50 named licenses would be included and 30 more would be extra if every agent needs the tool.


### Overage charges


The same article explains overages. Five9 finds the highest number of active users in a month and charges the difference between that peak and the licenses paid for. The[quality management article](https://documentation.five9.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-knowledgearticles1/page/kA6TN0000006gvp0AA.html) describes the same rule and says deactivating users who have left is the customer's job. The rate for an overage is not published.


### Usage-based charges


- **AI:** a footnote lists 3,000 minutes per bundled seat, plus usage.
- **SMS:** a footnote says SMS usage charges apply.
- **Workflow automation:** marked as subject to additional usage-based pricing.
- **Calling minutes and phone numbers:** no rates are published on the pricing page.


### Adapters, supervisors and add-ons


Core and above include a choice of CRM and UC adapters. The CRM options listed are Salesforce, ServiceNow, Dynamics, Zendesk or Oracle. The UC options are Microsoft Teams, Zoom, RingCentral and ATT Office@hand. Five9's knowledge article says supervisor licenses are no longer free and that more are bought through the account team.


The pricing page lists further add-ons without prices: the Intelligent Virtual Agent, AI Agents, Agent Assist, Aceyus dashboards, Five9 Analytics, customer success bundles and a technical account manager.


### Contract terms


Contract length, billing frequency, renewal and cancellation terms are not published on the pricing page. Ask for them in the quote, along with the seat price for each bundle, the usage rates and the cost of extra named licenses.


## Who Five9 fits and who it does not


Five9 describes its product as a cloud contact center with bundles a buyer can tailor. It fits a contact center with at least 50 agents logged in at once that needs voice and digital channels in one system. Its[dialer page](https://www.five9.com/products/capabilities/dialer-system) lists predictive, progressive, power and preview dialers and a manual touch mode, which suits outbound teams that need several modes.


It also fits centers that run shifts. Concurrent licensing means part-time and rotating agents can share seats. The Pro and Enterprise bundles fit a buyer who wants quality management and workforce management from the same vendor.


Five9 is a weaker fit for a team with fewer than 50 seats, since the listed prices carry that minimum. It is also a weaker fit for a buyer who wants to start with a card and a trial, or who needs a full price list before talking to sales. A sales team that only wants to dial from lists in its CRM would be buying far more than a dialer.

## Frequently asked questions


### How much does Five9 cost per user?


Five9's pricing page lists Digital at $119 and Core at $159 per concurrent user a month, with a minimum of 50 seats. Digital has no voice. Plus, Pro and Enterprise have no published price. The page says usage-based pricing may apply on top of the seat price.


### What does concurrent user mean on Five9?


A concurrent user is a seat that one agent at a time can occupy. Five9's documentation says a domain with 10 licenses lets 10 agents log in at the same time, and the 11th is refused. A team buys enough seats for its peak number of logged-in agents, not for every person on the roster.


### Does Five9 have a seat minimum?


Yes. The note under the bundles on Five9's pricing page states a minimum of 50 seats for the listed prices. At $159 a seat, 50 Core seats come to $7,950 a month at list price before usage. Five9 also mentions named-agent and pay-per-use options, which are quoted.


### Does Five9 offer a free trial?


Five9's pricing page does not list a free trial or a way to buy online. Every bundle has a quote button, and the page asks buyers to contact a Five9 representative. Ask Five9 directly if a pilot matters to your evaluation.


### Which Five9 plans are quote-only?


Plus, Pro and Enterprise. Plus adds AI Agent Assist and AI Knowledge to Core. Pro adds quality management, workforce management and analytics. Enterprise includes both sets. Add-ons such as AI Agents and the Intelligent Virtual Agent are also listed without prices.


### What costs extra on Five9?


The pricing page names SMS usage, AI usage on top of 3,000 minutes per bundled seat, and workflow automation usage. Named workforce licenses beyond the concurrent seat count are sold as add-ons, and Five9's documentation describes monthly overage charges for them. None of these rates is published.
